subject: history_social
passage: Lalbagh Fort in Dhaka, Bangladesh, was begun in 1678 by a Mughal prince but was never finished. Visitors today can still see three main ______ a mosque, a tomb, and an audience hall with a bathhouse. Beyond these, much of what the builders planned, including the walls that would have enclosed a far larger complex, was simply abandoned.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Visitors today can still see three main structures" is a complete sentence. "A mosque, a tomb, and an audience hall with a bathhouse" is not a clause but a list naming those three structures. A colon placed after a complete sentence introduces such a list.
explanation.A: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the list runs into the sentence with nothing to connect it to "three main structures."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Which" introduces a clause with a verb, but "a mosque, a tomb, and an audience hall" is only a list of nouns, so "which" has nothing to attach to.
explanation.C: Correct. A colon after the complete sentence introduces the list of the three structures.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on each side; the list that follows is not a clause.
